answer: Matplotlib already exposes a comparable version tuple: `matplotlib.__version_info__`. It is a `_VersionInfo` namedtuple, built by `_parse_to_version_info` from `__version__` and modelled on `sys.version_info`. It is defined lazily in the module-level `__getattr__` class.
Artist.format_cursor_data now special-cases BoundaryNorm. It uses the norm's boundaries to compute the delta, so it no longer calls the non-invertible norm.inverse.

The IndexError came from RangeSlider's polygon having only 4 vertices when the initial values were equal (e.g. valinit=[0, 0]), so `xy[4]` was out of bounds. The fix is to create the polygon with 5 vertices up front, `Polygon(np.zeros([5, 2]), **kwargs)`. The vertices, including the closing vertex 4, are then updated in `_update_selection_poly`. That helper is called from `__init__` and `set_val`, and it replaces the old `xy[4] = ...` lines in `set_val`.

Axes3D.draw in lib/mpl_toolkits/mplot3d/axes3d.py now starts with `if not self.get_visible(): return`, so `set_visible(False)` is respected. Axes3D overrides `draw` and does not call the base-class `_AxesBase.draw`. Before this check, it drew the axes even when they were not visible. I read the code but did not run the reproduction script.

rc_context saved/restored the 'backend' rcParam; restoring the auto-backend sentinel made a later get_backend() (rcParams['backend']) trigger plt.switch_backend, closing all figures. Fix: in rc_context, snapshot `orig = dict(rcParams.copy())` and `del orig['backend']` so backend is not restored on exit.

The bug was fixed in Poly3DCollection.get_facecolor (and get_edgecolor). `_facecolors2d` is only set in do_3d_projection. If it isn't set yet, the getter now sets `self.axes.M = self.axes.get_proj()` and calls `do_3d_projection()` before returning `np.asarray(self._facecolors2d)`.

Figure.__getstate__ must discard the device-pixel-ratio-scaled dpi by pickling the original dpi: `state["_dpi"] = state.get('_original_dpi', state['_dpi'])` (otherwise the canvas re-created in __setstate__ records the already doubled dpi as _original_dpi and scales it again).

Legend.__init__ already accepts a `draggable` keyword (default False). It is documented at legend.py:388, and the constructor applies it with `self.set_draggable(state=draggable)`. This was added in PR #23913, "Add draggable as param to Legend init", which closed this issue (#9181) in 3.7.0.

In Line3D.set_3d_properties (called via line_2d_to_3d after the class is already switched to Line3D), np.broadcast_to(zs, len(xs)) raises when given array input, so `self._verts3d` is never assigned. The half-converted Line3D stays on the axes and later draw() fails with "no attribute '_verts3d'".

The warning is emitted in Figure.subplots_adjust when the figure has a layout engine with adjust_compatible False. The cause is Figure.__init__ setting the 'constrained' layout engine even when constrained_layout=False (check `is not None` instead of truthiness; fixed by `elif constrained_layout:` around figure.py:2503).

The StopIteration comes from `_safe_first_finite` in cbook.py. It calls `next()` on a generator that only yields finite values, so an all-NaN x raises when nothing is finite. `Axes._convert_dx` calls it and doesn't catch StopIteration. The line in this checkout already has the fix: `next((val for val in obj if safe_isfinite(val)), safe_first_element(obj))`. If no finite value exists, it falls back to the first element. I did not run the reproduction.

The code in this checkout no longer has the crash. The old code looped over `curr_stream` (`for ps_name, xs_names in stream`). With an empty line, `curr_stream` stayed `None` and the unpack failed. `draw_text` now builds a flat `stream` list of `(ps_name, x, char_name)` and loops over it with `itertools.groupby`. An empty string gives an empty `stream`, so the loop body never runs and nothing is unpacked from `None`. The `groupby` loop at line 651 is the fixed version of the code that crashed. I didn't run the reproduction script.

Axis.set_ticks in matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/axis.py already handles this. If kwargs are passed without labels (labels is None), it raises ValueError('labels argument cannot be None when kwargs are passed'). When labels are given, the kwargs are validated as Text properties by set_ticklabels. The secondary axis and colorbar set_ticks methods pass kwargs through to this method, so they get the same check.

The KeyError comes from how `style.library` is built. `read_style_directory` keys each style by its file name (`styles[path.stem]`). In 3.6 the seaborn style files were renamed to `seaborn-v0_8-*`, so the key `seaborn-colorblind` no longer exists. Use `seaborn-v0_8-colorblind` instead.

The upstream fix for this issue (PRs #24265 and #24270, in 3.6.2) restored the old names in `library` and warned on use. That shim isn't in this checkout. The `seaborn-<foo>` styles have since been removed completely (`doc/api/next_api_changes/removals/25456-AL.rst`). I didn't find the `mplstyle` files themselves, because `list_files` returned nothing for the `stylelib` folder.

The warnings come from Colormap.__call__ assigning _i_over/_i_under/_i_bad (N+1, N, N+2) into a uint8 array. The fix is to compute the masks first and cast xa to int before the assignments: `xa = xa.astype(int)`, so the assignments at lines 741-743 no longer overflow.

The bug comes from `DraggableBase` keeping a direct reference to the figure canvas. A canvas such as `FigureCanvasQTAgg` can't be pickled, so pickling a figure with a draggable legend or annotation fails.

The code here already has the fix, and I haven't run the reproduction script to confirm it. `canvas` is now a read-only property that looks up `self.ref_artist.figure.canvas` on each access. It is no longer stored as an instance attribute, so the canvas stays out of the pickled state. The callbacks are also registered with `_connect_picklable` on the figure's `_canvas_callbacks`, so the registry itself can be pickled too.

The pickling failure comes from `Grouper`, which `align_labels()` fills through `figure._align_label_groups`. It stores its members in a `WeakKeyDictionary` of `WeakSet`s, and weak references can't be pickled. `Grouper.__getstate__` is the fix: it converts the weak references to strong ones, and `__setstate__` converts them back. I haven't run the reproduction script.

The bug was in DraggableBase.disconnect in offsetbox.py. It called self.canvas.mpl_disconnect(cid), and `canvas` is a property that reads self.ref_artist.figure.canvas. Once the artist is removed, its figure is None, so that raised AttributeError. The code now stores `_disconnectors` (partials of callbacks.disconnect on the figure's `_canvas_callbacks`) and `disconnect` calls those. It no longer goes through the canvas, so it works when figure is None.

The `ZeroDivisionError` happens because the new `LogNorm()` has `vmin` and `vmax` set to `None` when the colorbar redraws. In this code, `Colorbar._process_values` handles that: it calls `self.mappable.autoscale_None()` before the norm is used, so the norm is scaled from the mappable's data first. If the norm is still unscaled, it falls back to 0 and 1. `update_normal` also detects that `mappable.norm` differs from the colorbar's norm and resets the locator, formatter and scale. I read this code but did not run your example.

`update_bruteforce` no longer exists in this code. Assigning `plot.norm = LogNorm()` already triggers `changed()` through the norm setter in `cm.py`, and `cb.update_normal(plot)` redraws the colorbar with the new norm.

The line I'm submitting is the autoscale call in `_process_values`.

This is my best guess, and I did not confirm it. I ran out of tool calls before I could trace the failure end to end. The likely cause is in `Colorbar._process_values`. When the norm is unscaled, it forces `self.norm.vmin = 0` and `self.norm.vmax = 1`. A `LogNorm` can't have a vmin of 0, so the next `LogNorm.__call__` raises "Invalid vmin or vmax". I couldn't find where the norm becomes unscaled in your example. The reproduction sets `LogNorm(1, 5)`, which is already scaled. The error is raised at `matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/colors.py:1721`.

The error comes from `_tick_only`, which assumes `ax.axis` is subscriptable. That holds for `mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1.mpl_axes.Axes`, but not for other axes classes like `GeoAxes`, where `axis` is a plain method. `ax.axis["bottom"]` therefore raises `TypeError: 'method' object is not subscriptable`.

In Axis._set_lim (axis.py), shared sibling axes are updated with emit=False, so their xlim_changed/ylim_changed callbacks are never processed; only self.axes.callbacks.process is called inside `if emit:`. The fix is to also call other.callbacks.process(f"{name}lim_changed", other) for each shared sibling in that loop, keeping emit=False to avoid recursion.

The slider grabs the mouse on button press, and its on_changed callback runs while that grab is still held. The callback calls clf(), which removes the old Axes. If the removed Axes doesn't release the grab, `canvas.mouse_grabber` stays pointing at a dead Axes. Every later mouse event is then routed to it, so no widget receives input. A Button doesn't hit this because it releases the grab before firing `clicked`. The fix is in `Figure.delaxes`, which calls `self.canvas.release_mouse(ax)` when an Axes is removed. `Figure.clear` calls `delaxes` for each Axes. I read the code and did not run the reproduction. The release call is already present in this checkout, so the bug may already be fixed here, or it may come from somewhere I didn't find.

The backslash comes from `_escape_args_and_kwargs` in `sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py`. It rewrites a trailing `_` in a field name as `\_`. `_consume_field` calls it for every field, including attribute names. `_parse_attributes_section` then writes that escaped name straight into `.. attribute:: hello\_`. The escaping is conditional on `strip_signature_backslash`, and that condition already sits on the line I'm submitting. I did not run the repro, so I haven't confirmed which setting triggers it. I also didn't change any code.

The module template's `members` variable is populated in generate_autosummary_content via `ns['members'] = scanner.scan(imported_members)`, which uses ModuleScanner.scan (generate.py, lines 170-211) to filter out imported members when autosummary_imported_members is False.

Implemented via the new `man_make_section_directory` config option (default False). When enabled, the manpage builder creates `man<section>` directories (e.g. `man/man1/`) and writes each page to `man<section>/<name>.<section>`.

The split comes from the index sort key in `IndexEntries.create_index` (`keyfunc`), which decides where symbol entries go relative to letters. The older code prefixed letter and underscore keys with `chr(127)` and sorted everything else by its raw characters. `@` (U+0040) sorts below `chr(127)`, so it landed before the words. `£` (U+00A3) and `←` (U+2190) sort above it, so they landed after the words. The grouping step (`keyfunc3`) puts all of them under the same "Symbols" heading, but the two runs are not adjacent, so `groupby` emits two separate "Symbols" sections with the same anchor.

The code at this line already has the fix: a tuple sort key puts every non-letter, non-underscore entry in group 0, ahead of the words. I did not run a build to confirm the fix, and I did not find a separate remaining cause. The same `chr(127)` prefix is still used for sub-entries in `keyfunc2` (line 150), which doesn't affect the top-level sections.

The `autodoc_typehints = 'none'` check for overloaded functions is in `FunctionDocumenter.format_signature`. The condition `self.config.autodoc_typehints != 'none'` at line 1312 stops overload signatures from being used when the setting is `'none'`. In that case it falls back to `super().format_signature()`, which already honours the setting at line 1274. I only read the code and did not run the reproduction. The same guard is also at line 2188 for methods and line 1607 for classes. I did not open the class one.

autodoc_type_aliases is applied to variables/attributes by passing self.config.autodoc_type_aliases to get_type_hints in DataDocumenter.add_directive_header (and likewise in AttributeDocumenter.add_directive_header at line 2604, and the uninitialized-variable/attribute mixins).

The warning comes from `Cmdoption.handle_signature` in `sphinx/sphinx/domains/std.py` (line 153). It fires when `option_desc_re` doesn't match. That regex is defined at line 33 and is now `((?:/|--|-|\+)?[^\s=]+)(=?\s*.*)`. It no longer excludes `[` from the option name. For `[enable=]PATTERN` it matches `[enable` as the name and `=]PATTERN` as the args, so the warning no longer fires for this input. I didn't run it, only read the code.

The empty `__all__` case is handled in `ModuleDocumenter.get_object_members` in `sphinx/sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py`. It checks `if self.__all__ is None:` instead of `if not self.__all__:`. An empty list therefore goes to the `else` branch, which marks every member as skipped. Only a missing `__all__` documents all members. `inspect.getall` returns the empty list unchanged. I read the code but did not run the reproduction.

The warning comes from numref resolution: get_figtype() in the toctree env collector now skips uncaptioned nodes ("Skip if uncaptioned node"), so tables without a caption get no fignumber registered; a :numref: to such a table then hits get_fignumber() raising ValueError, and StandardDomain logs the "number is not assigned" warning. Fix: add a caption to the table (or use :ref: with explicit title).

The Struct problem comes from `struct.Struct.__module__` being `_struct` before Python 3.9, so autodoc emitted a reference that couldn't be resolved. The fix is the `INVALID_BUILTIN_CLASSES` mapping in `sphinx/util/typing.py`. It maps `Struct` to `'struct.Struct'` (and `TracebackType` to `'types.TracebackType'`). `restify()` and `stringify_annotation()` both consult it through `is_invalid_builtin_class()`, so annotations render as `struct.Struct`.

_parse_other_parameters_section now checks napoleon_use_param: if true it renders with _format_docutils_params (as :param:/:type: fields), otherwise it uses _format_fields('Other Parameters', ...). That is the same as _parse_parameters_section.

This is already supported in the code. `inherited_members_option` splits the `:inherited-members:` value on commas into a set of class names, so you can write `Base, list`. In `is_filtered_inherited_member`, a member is skipped when it comes from any class in the MRO whose name is in that set. A bare `:inherited-members:` maps to `{'object'}`. I read the code but did not run it. A test using `'Base, list'` exists in `tests/test_ext_autodoc_automodule.py`.

The module pages come from `collect_pages` in `sphinx/sphinx/ext/viewcode.py`, which is the `html-collect-pages` handler. The fix is its `is_supported_builder(app.builder)` guard at line 228. That guard calls `is_supported_builder` (lines 59-66), which returns False for epub builders when `viewcode_enable_epub` is False. I did not run a build to confirm this.

`doctree_read` still collects `env._viewcode_modules` during a `make html epub` run, because the environment is shared between the two builders. That is why the guard in `collect_pages` is what stops the epub pages. The code I read already contains this check, so I could not find a spot where it is missing.

In `modify_field_list` in sphinx/sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py, the `*args` and `**kwargs` branches rename `name` but never assign `arg`. The code calls `arguments.get(name)` and discards the result. Only the final `else` sets `arg = arguments.get(name, {})`. So the `*name` and `**name` branches never see the documented `param` and `type` entries. As a result, `modify_field_list` adds duplicate `type args` / `param args` fields and the same for `kwargs`. The fix is to replace `arguments.get(name)` with `arg = arguments.get(name, {})` in both branches, or to compute `arg` once after the `name` adjustment. I haven't edited the file or run anything.

The bug is in `docinfo_re = re.compile(':\\w+:.*?')`. `prepend_prolog` uses it to find the docinfo (field list) at the top of a document. It also matches a title line that starts with a role, such as ":mod:`mypackage2`". The prolog is then inserted after that title line instead of before it. That separates the heading from its underline and breaks the heading.

The code that handles this is `get_class_members` in `sphinx/sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py`. For annotation-only members, it looks up the `#:` comment in the analyzer of the class that declares them (`Foo` here), keyed by `(qualname, name)`. It then attaches that comment to the member as its docstring. `filter_members` uses that docstring, so a superclass attribute like `Foo.attr1` is no longer treated as undocumented.

I only read the code and did not run the example. I couldn't find a flaw in this path, so the repo may already include the fix. The cited line is the lookup that does the fix's work.

The bug is in SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects in requests/requests/sessions.py. Each loop iteration begins with `prepared_request = req.copy()`, which copies the original request. A method change from an earlier redirect, such as 303 turning POST into GET, is lost, so a later 307 re-sends the original POST. I haven't tested a fix. The fix is to copy the previous request on each iteration and not the original. For example, set `req = prepared_request` at the end of the loop, or keep the current request in a variable that is updated each iteration.

The fix is already in the code. `Request.__init__` calls `register_hook` for each hooks entry (models.py:222-223). `RequestHooksMixin.register_hook` accepts either a single callable or an iterable of callables. For an iterable, it extends the hook list with the callable items, so a list is no longer wrapped in another list. I haven't run it.

Raw socket.error during body read is caught in urllib3's response _error_catcher (`except (HTTPException, SocketError)`) and re-raised as ProtocolError, which requests' iter_content then wraps as ChunkedEncodingError (models.py:670-671).

This code already wraps both exceptions. In `Response.iter_content`, `generate()` catches urllib3's `DecodeError` and raises `ContentDecodingError`. In the same block, urllib3's `ReadTimeoutError` becomes `ConnectionError`. In `adapters.py`, a `ReadTimeoutError` raised while sending is converted to `ReadTimeout` (line 493). A connect timeout that arrives wrapped in `MaxRetryError` becomes `ConnectTimeout` (line 473). The `DecodeError` handler is at the cited line. I didn't run anything to confirm a proxy timeout takes one of these paths.

With decode_unicode=True, iter_content only decodes when r.encoding is set. For application/json with no charset in the Content-Type header, get_encoding_from_headers returns None (it only defaults to ISO-8859-1 for 'text' types). In that case stream_decode_response_unicode yields the raw bytes unchanged. r.text doesn't have this problem because it falls back to the detected encoding (apparent_encoding/chardet). To get unicode from iter_content, set r.encoding (for example 'utf-8') before iterating.

The `builtin_str(method)` call isn't in this checkout. `sessions.py` no longer converts the method. `Session.request` only calls `method.upper()` (line 452). The conversion now happens in `PreparedRequest.prepare_method`, which calls `to_native_string(self.method.upper())`. `to_native_string` decodes a bytes method like `b'GET'` to the native string `'GET'`. It doesn't produce the literal `"b'GET'"` that `builtin_str(b'GET')` gave on Python 3. This means a bytes method from neutronclient's `safe_encode_list` works on Python 3.
Blueprint.__init__ raises ValueError("'name' may not contain a dot '.' character.") when the blueprint name contains a dot.

Flask already supports this through a `text: bool = True` parameter on `Config.from_file()`, not a `mode` string. Passing `text=False` opens the file in binary mode: `app.config.from_file("config.toml", tomllib.load, text=False)`. The mode is chosen in `open(filename, "r" if text else "rb")`.

The `flask routes` command is `routes_command` in flask/src/flask/cli.py. It builds a table of only Endpoint, Methods and Rule, so it never shows the subdomain. Adding a Domain column would mean changing this function. Its headers, widths and row format are at lines 1021-1034, and the rows are printed in the loop at line 1033-1034.

To get the subdomain data without changing Flask, read `current_app.url_map.iter_rules()`. Each rule has a `subdomain` attribute. The domain is `f"{rule.subdomain}.{SERVER_NAME}"` when the subdomain is set, and `SERVER_NAME` alone when it is empty.
